## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish-brown wings with curved darker crosslines, subtle pale shading, and a bark- or leaf-litter-like resting pattern. In Florida, the Curved-lined Owlet is likely found in warm wooded, shrubby, or semi-open habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, yards, and weedy areas where adults may come to lights. Its caterpillar host plants appear poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small nocturnal plant-feeding moth whose larvae likely feed on low vegetation or plant debris while supporting birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
